stories.text: Ruddington's station on the Great Central Railway opened on 15 March 1899.[^s1] From 1940 a depot was built here to fill and store ammunition, and it closed in 1983.[^s2] The station had closed in 1963, and the Nottingham Heritage Railway now runs trains on the line.[^s1] The rest of the depot's land is a business park and Rushcliffe Country Park.[^s1][^s2]

Former Framework Knitters Workshop Now Part Of Museum Complex, East Block

stories.text: In about 1829 cottages were built for Ruddington's framework knitters, who worked at hand frames in workshops behind them; the workshops date from about 1840. All are listed, and together they now make up the Framework Knitters' Museum.

23365.sum: The building dates from about 1840, according to Historic England (via Wikipedia). It is Grade II listed as Former Framework Knitters' Workshop Now Part of Museum Complex, East Block.

stories.text: Around 1292–94 a manor chapel, St Mary's, was founded in the village. It took the name of St Peter's from the old parish church at Flawford when that was pulled down in the 1770s.

24245.sum: St. Peter's Church is a Church of England church in Ruddington, Nottinghamshire.

stories.text: In 1860 Thomas Cross, a banker from Bolton, built the hall. From 1880 it was the home of Philo Laos Mills, an American merchant who became High Sheriff of Nottinghamshire. In the Second World War it became a hospital, and it stayed one until 1980.

319097.sum: Ruddington Hall is a country house standing in the grounds of a garden in Ruddington, Nottinghamshire, England. Ruddington Hall has been included in the art work of Nikolaus Pevsner alongside the Elizabethan Wollaton Hall and Newstead Abbey, ancestral home of Lord Byron. Pevsner described it as having a classical ethic of "calm grandeur, and monumental simplicity".
